title: Sunny and the Sleepy Wombat
author: Jamie Wigg
the_end_text:
The End.
Sweet dreams, little one. Goodnight.
back_cover_blurb: As evening settles over the bush, Sunny the little quokka meets a round, sleepy wombat who shows her his warm burrow beneath the old gum tree. Together they say goodnight to the moon. A calm, cosy bedtime tale for winding down and drifting off to sleep. Perfect for little ones ages 1-5.

pages.scene: the little quokka wandering past a big old gum tree in the soft blue evening, ears up, hearing a gentle snuffle; warm honey light fading, first stars
pages.text: In the soft blue evening, Sunny wandered by the old gum tree. Snuffle, snuffle — what was that?

pages.scene: a round sturdy wombat with soft grey-brown fur, small round ears and a broad gentle sleepy face, waddling slowly out from beneath the gum tree roots, blinking; the little quokka watching
pages.text: Out waddled a round little wombat, blinking his sleepy eyes.

pages.scene: the round grey-brown wombat giving a big wide yawn, the little quokka smiling beside him, cosy dusk meadow
pages.text: He opened his mouth and gave a big, wide, wobbly yawn.

pages.scene: the little quokka and the round wombat meeting nose to nose, gentle and friendly, soft evening light, fireflies beginning
pages.text: “Hello,” said Sunny. The wombat blinked back, warm and kind.

pages.scene: a sweet portrait of the round sturdy wombat, soft grey-brown fur, broad gentle face, sleepy half-closed eyes, the little quokka beside him in the grass
pages.text: He was round and sturdy, soft and grey, with the gentlest, sleepiest face.

pages.scene: the round wombat turning and waddling slowly toward the base of the old gum tree, the little quokka following, moonlight beginning
pages.text: “Come and see my home,” he said, and waddled slowly on.

pages.scene: the entrance of a cosy burrow tunnel going down beneath the roots of the old gum tree, warm and inviting, the wombat leading the little quokka inside
pages.text: Down a round little tunnel, beneath the old gum tree's roots.

pages.scene: inside a warm snug earthy burrow softly lined with dry grass and leaves, cosy golden glow, the wombat and the little quokka looking around
pages.text: Inside was a warm, snug burrow, soft with dry grass and leaves.

pages.scene: the deep quiet cosy burrow, dim and safe and warm, the little quokka gazing around in wonder, the round wombat content
pages.text: Deep and quiet and safe — the cosiest place of all.

pages.scene: the round wombat curling up round as a stone in his burrow, warm and calm, the little quokka watching fondly
pages.text: The wombat curled up, round as a smooth grey stone.

pages.scene: the sleepy wombat snug in his burrow with eyes half closed, the little quokka sitting beside him, soft warm light
pages.text: “This is where I sleep all through the day,” he said softly.

pages.scene: view from near the burrow entrance of a silver moon rising over the old gum tree in a deep starry sky, calm and beautiful
pages.text: Outside, the moon rose silver over the old gum tree.

pages.scene: the little quokka and the round wombat peeking out from the burrow entrance together at the gentle moonlit night
pages.text: Together they peeked out at the soft and gentle night.

pages.scene: glowing fireflies drifting over the moonlit grass outside the gum tree, the little quokka and wombat watching quietly, peaceful
pages.text: Fireflies drifted by. The whole world was soft and still.

pages.scene: the round wombat yawning again and the little quokka yawning too, both sleepy and cosy near the burrow, moonlight
pages.text: The wombat yawned again — and Sunny yawned as well.

pages.scene: the little quokka and the round wombat looking up at the bright round moon and whispering goodnight, tender and calm
pages.text: “Goodnight, moon,” they whispered up to the sky.

pages.scene: the round wombat settling deep and cosy into his warm burrow, safe and snug, eyes closing
pages.text: The wombat settled deep in his warm and cosy burrow.

pages.scene: the little quokka padding home through cool quiet moonlit grass, sleepy and content, stars and a soft moon above
pages.text: And Sunny padded home through the cool and quiet grass.

pages.scene: the little quokka curling into her own soft nest of leaves and grass, warm and snug, under a calm starry sky
pages.text: She curled into her own soft nest, warm and safe and snug.

pages.scene: the little quokka fast asleep with a gentle smile, dreaming, the round moon glowing softly above, a tiny sleepy wombat dozing in the distant burrow
pages.text: Her eyes fell closed. She dreamed of the moon and a round, sleepy friend.
